faq.a: Sanaa is associated with the Arabic form صَنَاء, whose core sense is sanaa; the capital of yemen.

faq.q: What is the origin of Sanaa?
faq.a: Sanaa is associated with Arabic. Sanaa is Arabic صَنْعَاء (Ṣanʿāʾ), the name of the capital of Yemen, used as a female given name.
Yes — the underlying form صَنَاء is Arabic.
Sanaa can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Sanaa should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Ṣanʿāʾ is a place name, not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Sanaa mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Sanaa is rendered صناء and carries the sense صناء، یمن کا دارالحکومت.

faq.q: What does Sanaa mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Sanaa is rendered صنعا and carries the sense صنعا، پایتخت یمن.
A romanized syllable approximation is sa-naa. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Sanaa?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Sanaa, sana, sanaa. Script forms are صناء, صنعا, صنعاء, صَنَاء, सना.

faq.q: Is Sanaa a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
